subject.title: Expose maxMissedJobsPerRestart and missedJobStaggerMs in cron config

question: Should OpenClaw expose public cron restart catch-up controls, and should the supported API be raw max/stagger knobs, an explicit skip/freshness policy, or no new public config?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but public cron config changes upgrade behavior and scheduled-message semantics, and the requested disable behavior does not fall out of the current internal max/stagger implementation.

options.title: Design explicit catch-up policy
options.body: Add public config whose semantics distinguish run, stagger, and skip or maximum-age behavior instead of exposing raw internals unchanged.

options.title: Expose raw global knobs
options.body: Expose maxMissedJobsPerRestart and missedJobStaggerMs directly, but document that they tune immediate catch-up and do not by themselves skip all missed runs unless the runtime semantics are changed.

options.title: Keep controls internal
options.body: Decline new public config and document the current fixed catch-up behavior plus safer cron authoring patterns.

recommendation.title: Design explicit catch-up policy
recommendation.body: Add public config whose semantics distinguish run, stagger, and skip or maximum-age behavior instead of exposing raw internals unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to both the original internal controls and recent cron/config surface work.
